P02-roof-storm-e14-hero:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset: one standalone, full-size portrait painted environment background for Six Flights, Friday 6:50 storm, exact 3:4 portrait (e.g. 1086 × 1448 or larger native resolution). No captions, labels, type, borders from the reference board, or additional panels. Reference image 1 is the accepted A3 rooftop, for the recognizable rooftop geography and loose matte gouache and blue-black ink style only: DO NOT retain its canopy or dark screen. Reference image 2 is the storm contact sheet; use only the requested single thumbnail as cloud composition reference, and create a new high-detail painting, not an upscaled crop. Reference image 3 is existing P02 storm A, for production staging and size of the screen/quiet floor. Paint on lightly textured cream notebook paper with ragged dry-brush perimeter like P02, subdued chalky broad gouache strokes and restrained ink edges. Hong Kong harbour skyline with sparse subdued amber window dots, distant hills, concrete parapet, familiar rusted cylindrical water tank on its frame on far left, the concrete stairhead and closed dark door on far right. In center, a single upright head-on off-white matte screen framed on two narrow poles, simple nearly straight 5:3 fabric rectangle with no tilt, from around x27–73%, y43–64%. The SCREEN is the brightest object, soft even off-white fabric with very subtle surface texture, blank, not glowing. Keep the bottom 29% as even dark blue-black concrete, empty and calm for live cutouts and overlays. No tarp, cables, chairs, audience, people, projector, equipment, writing, lamps, falling rain or rain streaks, bolts, bright puddles, reflections, beams, cast-light patches, projected image, or visible special effects. Cool limited indigo, graphite, and slate palette, no saturated character accent colours.
Cloud direction: study E14, top row second panel. One huge, convex, inky indigo-gray cloud bulges from the upper-left corner and hangs low over the city on the left. Its descending curved edge opens onto a receding pocket of subdued silver-gray sky on the right. Read it as one distinct advancing mass with a legible curved silhouette, layered smaller brush marks only at its perimeter; do not paint diagonal streaks or evenly spaced stripes. Quiet tense scale contrast between that vast advancing storm and the little clean screen. The opening remains distinctly darker than the screen.

P02-roof-storm-e23-hero: Use case: illustration-story. Paint one original standalone production-ready matte gouache rooftop environment for Six Flights, Friday 6:50 just before the storm. Native 3:4 PORTRAIT, e.g. 1086×1448; not a crop or upsample. Use image 1 (accepted A3) for physical geography and medium only, not its tarp/dark screen. Use image 2 (storm board) only for the ideas in E23: a broken shelf of dense cloud on the left with a breathing pale slate-grey slit on the horizon to its right. Do NOT clone the reference board composition. An intentionally different camera position: a small backward step and sideways move to the LEFT, looking across the same rooftop as if someone has just come out to check the sky. The tank still sits at far left, perceptibly larger and closer to us, and the same small right stairhead with closed blue-black door is a little farther away, all coherent gently receding perspective. Fit it all within frame with the left tank partly inset. Screen stands slightly RIGHT of center, not perfectly centered, projected canvas centered at x54%, y52% with a useful blank fabric rectangle about 43% wide × 19% tall, off-white, brightest but not lit, two dark skinny poles. Camera remains close to perpendicular to screen so it is nearly rectangular and can be composited; keep it clear of other silhouettes. Give stage more room: at least bottom 35% quiet empty very dark matte concrete, with broad near-uniform muted slate-indigo wash. Skyline a thin legible Hong Kong harbour strip with sparse warm window pinpoints. No audience, props, projector, beams, screen illumination, movie, atmospheric beams, rain streaks, light on floor, puddles, reflections, lightning, lamps, tarp, cords, chairs, text or title, and no saturated character colours. Atmospheric direction: small horizontal opening of subdued bluish silver LOW above the right skyline; high upper sky is quieter near-flat slate as contrast to scumbled dark scalloped horizontal storm shelf unfurling left-to-right LOW, rather than E14's looming big top-left diagonal cloud or E18's repeated bands. Distinct strong negative space at top, believable scale. Match A3's flat pigment, visible paper, soft pools, restrained spare blue-black ink, chalky expressive hand-painted shapes. Avoid heavy impasto and swirly repetitive artificial brush texture; finer quieter surface especially on the screen. Thin irregular cream deckled paper edge, NOT a broad frame.
